newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: News conference planned on Zaire peace talks.
newsitem.headline: News conference planned on Zaire peace talks.

text.p: Zairean peace negotiators began a fourth day of talks in South Africa on Tuesday while fighting went on in Zaire, and South Africa's Foreign Ministry said a news conference would be held in Pretoria at 3.30 p.m. (1330 GMT).
There was no immediate indication of who would address the news conference or what it would be about.
"They met for an hour for direct talks early this morning," a Foreign Ministry spokesman told reporters without elaborating.
The parties themselves and the United Nations, represented at the talks at a secret venue by Organisation of African Unity envoy Mohamed Sahnoun, have been silent.
The talks began with a frosty public handshake in the South African government headquarters in Pretoria on Saturday between the leaders of the delegations.
Residents in Zaire's second largest city and copperbelt capital of Lubumbashi on Tuesday were expecting rebel forces of Laurent Kabila to march in at any moment.
Fighting was heard on the outskirts late on Monday and early on Tuesday but soldiers loyal to President Mobutu Sese Seko said they had repulsed the rebels.
